{{Short description|Dutch physicist}}
'''Alfons van Blaaderen''' (born 27 October 1963) is a Dutch physicist. He is a professor at [[Utrecht University]] and works in the field of [[soft matter]].<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=http://www.uu.nl/staff/AvanBlaaderen |title=prof. dr. A. (Alfons) van Blaaderen |language=Dutch |publisher=Utrecht University |date= |accessdate=16 November 2016}}</ref>

==Career==
Van Blaaderen was born on 27 October 1963 in [[Naarden]].<ref name=uu>{{cite web|author= |url=https://profs.library.uu.nl/index.php/profrec/getprofdata/105/1/1/0 |title=Prof.dr. A. van Blaaderen (1963 - ) |language=Dutch |publisher=Utrecht University |date= |accessdate=16 November 2016}}</ref> He attended the [[Voorbereidend wetenschappelijk onderwijs]] and subsequently studied physics and chemistry at Utrecht University. In 1992 he obtained his PhD at Utrecht University under professor A. Vrij with a dissertation titled ''Colloidal dispersions of (organo-)silica spheres: formation mechanism, structure and dynamics''. In 1999 he was named professor of experimental physics of [[condensed matter]].<ref name=uu/>

In 2011 Van Blaaderen was awarded the [[Peter Debye]] Prize by the Edmond Hustinx Foundation.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=http://www.fom.nl/live/english/news/archives/pressreleases2011/artikel.pag?objectnumber=142683 |title=Alfons van Blaaderen wins Peter Debye Prize |language=Dutch |publisher=Foundation for Fundamental Research on Matter |date=23 February 2011 |accessdate=16 November 2016}}</ref> Van Blaaderen was elected a member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2013.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/7952 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161116202112/https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/7952 |title=Alfons van Blaaderen |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |archive-date=16 November 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
